origin.description: Create a regular zoo series, the analogue of ts.
origin.usage: zooreg(data, start = 1, end = numeric(), frequency = 1, deltat = 1, ts.eps = getOption("ts.eps"), order.by = NULL, calendar = getOption("zoo.calendar", TRUE))

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: A vector, matrix, or factor. Missing data is a single logical NA.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: Time of the first observation. A length-two vector is a time unit and a 1-based sample within it.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: Time of the last observation, in the same form as start. Used as the anchor when start is missing.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Observations per unit of time. When deltat is also supplied, deltat is not replaced by 1/frequency.

arguments.name: deltat
arguments.text: Step between observations. Used as the index step even after a near-integer frequency is rounded.

arguments.name: ts.eps
arguments.text: Frequencies closer than this are treated as equal. The default is 1e-5.

arguments.name: order.by
arguments.text: When not NULL, start and end are ignored and zoo(data, order.by, frequency) is called. calendar on zooreg is not forwarded.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.text: If true, a numeric index with frequency 4 or 12 becomes yearqtr or yearmon.

origin.details: A missing frequency becomes 1/deltat. Otherwise a missing deltat becomes 1/frequency before a frequency greater than 1 is rounded to the nearest integer when it is within ts.eps. The grid is start + (0, 1, ...) * deltat, then snapped with floor(frequency * time + 0.0001) / frequency when start * frequency is an integer within ts.eps squared. Both start and end may be supplied; the index is still anchored at start, and end is only the check that start is not after end.
origin.value: A zooreg object, which is a zoo with a frequency attribute.
origin.example:
x <- zooreg(1:4, start = c(1959, 2), frequency = 4)
cat(paste(as.character(index(x)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(frequency(x), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Create a regular zoo series, the analogue of ts.
translation.usage: zooreg(data, start=1, end=None, frequency=1, deltat=1, ts_eps=1e-5, order_by=None, calendar=True)

arguments.name: data
arguments.text: A list, array, factor, or DataFrame. Omit it for one logical NA.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: First time. A pair (unit, sample) is unit + (sample - 1) / frequency. The default is 1.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: Last time. When start is omitted, the grid is anchored here.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Observations per unit of time. Rounded after deltat is frozen.

arguments.name: deltat
arguments.text: Index step. When frequency is supplied and deltat is not, this is 1/frequency of the unrounded frequency.

arguments.name: ts_eps
arguments.text: Absolute tolerance for rounding frequency. The snap uses ts_eps squared.

arguments.name: order_by
arguments.text: When set, the series is built by zoo and calendar is left at zoo's default.

arguments.name: calendar
arguments.text: When true, frequency 4 or 12 stores a numeric index as yearqtr or yearmon.

translation.details: Missing start and end are detected before the defaults are substituted, so an omitted start is numeric 1 and is not an integer index. An integer start with an omitted end does store an integer index when the grid lands on integers. Frequency 4 and 12 use the yearqtr and yearmon encodings floor(4 * x + 0.001) / 4 and floor(12 * x + 0.0001) / 12.
translation.value: A Zoo with regular true and frequency set.
translation.example:
from zoo.zooreg import format_yearqtr, zooreg
import numpy as np
x = zooreg(np.arange(1, 5), start=(1959, 2), frequency=4)
print(" ".join(format_yearqtr(v) for v in np.asarray(x.index)))
print(int(x.frequency))
